text: According to simulation theory (Gordon, Goldman), we understand another person's mind primarily by:
choices: Applying an implicit folk-psychological theory of how mental states cause behavior
Directly perceiving their mental states in their expressive behavior
Inferring their mind by analogy from our own single case
Running our own cognitive and motivational system 'offline' from their perspective
explanation: Simulation theory holds that we model others by running our own cognitive/motivational system 'offline,' adopting their perspective, rather than consulting a theory. Applying an implicit theory is theory-theory; directly perceiving mental states in expression is interaction theory; and analogical inference from one's own case is the classical argument from analogy.
